title: Before You Say "I Do"... Answer These Questions First—or Risk Building Love on a Foundation That Cannot Survive
paragraphs:
Before You Say "I Do"... Answer These Questions First—or Risk Building Love on a Foundation That Cannot Survive
Marriage doesn't fail overnight. It usually begins with questions that were never asked, truths that were never spoken, and hearts that were never fully surrendered to Jesus Christ.
Some of the deepest heartbreaks in life do not begin with betrayal.
"We thought we wanted the same things."
Two people who once promised forever become strangers living under the same roof.
Not because they never loved each other.
But because they never truly knew each other.
Marriage was never designed to be sustained by chemistry alone.
God designed it to be built upon truth.
Before Adam and Eve became husband and wife, God established identity before relationship.
"Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh."
The word דָּבַק (dāvaq) means far more than simply "stay together."
Biblical marriage is not temporary attachment.
That kind of union requires honest conversations before vows are ever spoken.
Too many couples spend thousands planning one wedding day...
Yet spend almost no time preparing for fifty years of marriage.
"So they are no longer two but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate."
ὃ οὖν ὁ Θεὸς συνέζευξεν (ho oun ho Theos synezeuxen)
Before stepping under that yoke, every couple should courageously answer questions that reveal whether both hearts are truly walking toward Christ—or merely walking toward each other.
Do we both genuinely love Jesus Christ more than we love each other?
Because if Christ is not first...
"Seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness..."
A Christ-centered marriage begins with two surrendered disciples—not merely two compatible personalities.
"Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you."
The Greek word for forgive is:
Biblical forgiveness is literally giving grace.
Marriage without grace becomes a courtroom.
Marriage with grace becomes a sanctuary.
Jesus spoke more about money than almost any other daily subject because money often reveals the true master of the heart.
What wounds from childhood are still unhealed?
Because marriage does not erase trauma.
Pretending pain never happened only invites it into the marriage.
How do we respond when one of us fails?
Very few prepare for the inevitable failures.
Marriage is not finding someone perfect.
It is promising to help each other become more like Christ.
How will we raise our children—if God blesses us with them?
Will your children learn that Jesus is merely important...
"These words... shall be on your heart. You shall teach them diligently to your children."
Parents do not merely tell children about God.
They sharpen their hearts toward Him every single day.
What does faithfulness truly mean to us?
Because adultery begins long before the affair.
"Everyone who looks at a woman lustfully has already committed adultery with her in his heart."
Biblical faithfulness begins where nobody else can see.
Can we confess sin to one another?
Healthy marriages are not built by pretending perfection.
They are built through humble repentance.
Who has permission to correct us?
"Faithful are the wounds of a friend."
Will we still choose each other?
Yet Scripture repeatedly points believers toward endurance.
Marriage vows are tested not during celebration...
These moments reveal whether the covenant was rooted in emotion...
Above every practical question stands one final question.
Perhaps the most important question of all.
Have we both truly surrendered our lives to Jesus Christ?
Because no amount of compatibility can substitute for genuine conversion.
No communication strategy can replace regeneration.
No relationship advice can transform a heart the Holy Spirit has not changed.
The Gospel is not merely preparation for marriage.
It is the foundation of marriage.
Jesus did not come simply to improve broken people.
He came to make dead sinners alive.
That is why our message has always been...

If you are dating, engaged, or even already married, don't rush past these questions. Sit down together. Open your Bible. Pray honestly. Answer with humility, not with the answers you think the other person wants to hear. A marriage rooted in truth may have difficult conversations today, but it is far less likely to experience devastating surprises tomorrow. God honors truth because He is truth.
If this article challenged you, don't keep it to yourself. Someone you love may be one honest conversation away from avoiding years of unnecessary heartache.

And if one of these questions exposed something your heart has been avoiding, be honest before God. Comment, "Jesus, search my heart," if you're willing to let Him prepare you for the covenant He designed. Your testimony may become the encouragement someone else desperately needs.
Every share helps extend biblical truth to people who may never walk into a church but may encounter Jesus through your testimony online.
Even more importantly, you'll gain access to ongoing biblical encouragement and discipleship.
One honest conversation today can become the testimony your children thank God for tomorrow.
